title: Scratch your own itch
coreMove: When you build to relieve a problem you personally feel, your own daily use becomes the test; firsthand pain gives sharper judgment than guessing at a stranger's needs.

exampleSpecs.audience: makers tempted to chase a market they do not share
exampleSpecs.stakes: build from felt pain or guess at an outsider's needs
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist chooses to solve a problem the team personally feels

exampleSpecs.audience: teams trusting surveys over lived friction
exampleSpecs.stakes: trust stated preferences or the friction you actually feel
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist weighs survey wishes against firsthand pain

exampleSpecs.audience: builders deciding whether to design tools in the abstract
exampleSpecs.stakes: design a framework up front or let real work produce one
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: value emerges as a by-product of solving a real problem

exampleSpecs.audience: makers mistaking personal love for proven demand
exampleSpecs.stakes: treat self-love as proof or as a hypothesis to test
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist separates personal taste from market demand

exampleSpecs.stakes: quit at the unglamorous middle or finish it well
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: self-felt need sustains effort when payout is uncertain

exampleSpecs.audience: makers checking whether their pain generalizes
exampleSpecs.stakes: assume the pain is shared or verify it before scaling
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist tests whether firsthand pain is common or idiosyncratic
